note: Authored online-intake cases. Each has a `seed` (tickets already in the window) and one `arriving` ticket, and asks what incremental correlation does with the arrival. Original content, no external dataset, no hidden labels in the ticket text. Small on purpose: this is acceptance and regression evidence, not a benchmark, and no broad claim should be made from eight cases.

records.scenario: Second reporter of the same auth failure, different words

seed.title: SSO sign-in returns invalid assertion for the whole team
seed.description: Nobody on our workspace can sign in through their identity provider since about 09:00. Every attempt returns an invalid assertion error.

seed.title: Cannot log in through our identity provider
seed.description: Sign-in through the identity provider is rejected for everyone on the workspace with an assertion error.

arriving.title: Sign-in through identity provider rejected, assertion error
arriving.description: Nobody on our workspace can sign in through the identity provider. Every attempt is rejected with an invalid assertion error.

records.note: Three reporters, one failure, overlapping vocabulary. LABEL CORRECTED while authoring: the expectation was 'attached', but the two seed tickets do not clear the linkage threshold with each other, so no candidate exists for the arrival to join — verified by correlating the seed alone, independently of what the arrival then did. Grouping the arrival with the compatible seed ticket and forming a candidate is the correct outcome. The case still earns its place: it shows a candidate forming on the third report rather than the second.

seed.title: Sync workers stuck, queue growing
seed.description: Connector sync jobs start and never finish. Queue depth is climbing and nothing completes.

arriving.title: Scheduled report queue is growing and jobs never complete

records.note: 'queue growing, never complete' matches lexically, but a different service and a different failure. A merge here would invent an incident.

records.scenario: Second compatible report promotes a singleton to a candidate

seed.title: Warehouse sync jobs stuck in running state
seed.description: Sync jobs start and never finish. The queue is growing and nothing completes.

arriving.title: Sync jobs stuck running, queue growing
arriving.description: Connector jobs start and never complete. Queue depth keeps climbing and nothing lands.

records.note: One report is a singleton; the second compatible one is what makes it an incident.

records.scenario: First report of the day, nothing to join

arriving.title: Dashboard exports are truncated
arriving.description: Our scheduled export stops partway through every run.

records.note: No active candidate exists. A lone report is a valid state, not a failure.
